messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: Hierarchical GAMs
parts:
Hi Everyone,

 

I am working on a problem for which I am trying to identify some non-linearity in the relationship between occupancy and a covariate.

In [JA][BU]GS I have successfully implemented some threshold / change point models, which are okay. However, I feel like being able to fit a GAM would be sensible thing to do.

 

So, my question is whether anyone has done this, i.e., a hierarchical occupancy model using a GAM?

 

I am just starting to look around, so apologies if there is an obvious solution that I haven’t found yet. Also, I wanted to crowdsource first, mostly to stimulate discussion.

 

Chris

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Hierarchical GAMs
parts:
Dear Chris,

we have an example of an occupancy model with splines of a covariate in both psi and p in the AHM1 book. End of chapter 10 or so.

Also, this paper use splines to model covariates in an occ model flexibly (our code in the book is from there):

Strebel, N., Kéry, M., Schaub , M., & Schmid, H. 2014. Study of phenology by flexible estimation and modeling of seasonal detectability peaks. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 5: 483–490.



Best regards  --  Marc

messages.subject: RE: Hierarchical GAMs
parts:
Well two things are confirmed:

 

1)       The brilliance of these groups

2)       My lack of basic reading before asking a question

 

Thanks everyone, that’s my weekend sorted!

 

Chris!

 

From: Duarte, Adam [mailto:adam.d...@gmail.com]
Sent: Thursday, December 8, 2016 1:02 PM
To: Kery Marc <marc...@vogelwarte.ch>; Chris SUtherland <chris...@gmail.com>; unma...@googlegroups.com; 'hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology' <hmec...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: Hierarchical GAMs

 

Hi Chris,

 

You might also check out Collier et al. (2012). They fit a geoadditive semiparametric occupancy model to warbler detection/non-detection data.



Collier, B.A., J. G. Groce, M. L. Morrison, J. C. Newnam, A. J. Campommizzi, S. L. Farrell, H. A. Mathewson, R. T. Snelgrove, R. J. Carroll, and R. N. Wilkins. 2012. Predicting patch occupancy in fragmented landscapes at the rangewide scale for endangered species: an example of an American warbler. Diversity and Distributions, 18: 158-167.



Cheers,



Adam
